newsitem.title: GERMANY: Focus - Hypo-Bank profits hit by risk cover.
newsitem.headline: Focus - Hypo-Bank profits hit by risk cover.

text.p: Shares in Germany's Hypo-Bank fell on Wednesday after the mortgage specialist said its 1996 operating profits fell nine percent because of a 50 percent increase in risk provisions.

Bayerische Hypotheken-und Wechsel-Bank AG 's shares dropped 1.90 marks, or 3.6 percent, to 55 marks in bourse trade, falling three times faster than the DAX index, which eased by 1.3 percent. The stock continued to decline in the after-bourse screen session.

In a preliminary earnings statement, Hypo-Bank said net operating income before provisions had risen 17 percent in 1996 and its recent consolidation of British fund manager Foreign & Colonial helped boost net commission income by 43 percent.

Nonetheless, it said the sharp rise in the need to cover against loan loss risks would mean final operating earnings drop substantially from 1.3 billion marks last year. It decided to hold its dividend at 1.45 marks.
Analysts, who were prepared for sharply higher risk provisions as Hypo-Bank had already made clear that its loan risks were rising, were still taken aback by the steepness of the jump.
"It's a worry for investors based on the current economic conditions in Germany and the weak outlook for the real-estate sector," said one analyst who declined to be named.
The results contrast with markedly better operating figures by Hypo-Bank's main rivals.

Market leader Deutsche Bank AG on Tuesday reported a 37 percent rise in operating income, albeit mostly stagnant net income. Operating income at Bayerische Vereinsbank, Hypo-Bank's closest rival, rose 18 percent.
Vereinsbank Research analyst Natalia Grasegger noted that while other banks had liquidated reserves to ease the impact of higher loan loss provisions, Hypo-Bank had opted not to do so.
But she noted that an expected low tax rate was likely to offset the impact of the provisions on Hypo's net earnings.
"I can't see this having a major long term impact. There are many other factors apart from fundamentals which are attracting interest to banking shares," she added.

Hypo-Bank, along with the rest of Germany's Big Five, has been attracting solid investor interest for months now ever since Deutsche Bank AG kicked off a wave of merger speculation by revealing a 5.2 percent stake in Bayerische Vereinsbank AG.
"Something is going to change in the banking sector and that is key," she said.

BHF Bank's Dieter Hein said Hypo-Bank's results were more positive than negative and said investors should not overlook the 21 percent increase in the bank's net commission income even without the consolidation of Foreign & Colonial (F&C).

Hypo-Bank also said its earnings from own-account trading rose to around 220 million marks from 192 million marks in 1996 while its net interest income rose about seven percent from last year's 4.1 billion marks.
The bank's balance sheet total rose to 339 billion marks from 299 billion in 1995 and lending volume increased 10 percent to 254 billion marks.
Administrative expenses increased by 4.5 percent, almost exclusively because of F&C, without which spending would have risen 0.2 percent, Hypo-Bank added. ($ = 1.693 German Marks)
